Case Study: A Parallelogram Flower Bed

Read the passage carefully, then answer the 5 MCQs in the test below.

A landscape designer is laying out a parallelogram-shaped flower bed in a public garden. Starting from a fixed corner peg she measures two edge directions in metres: one side runs along the vector u=(6,2) and the adjacent side along v=(1,4). She knows a neat fact from coordinate geometry — the exact area enclosed by two edge vectors drawn from the same point equals the absolute value of the 2×2 determinant whose columns are those vectors. Before ordering turf she wants three things settled: the area of the bed, what happens to the determinant if she lists the two edges in the opposite order, and whether a proposed change of the second edge would accidentally flatten the bed into a straight line of zero area. She treats every calculation exactly, without rounding.

questions.explanation: [6 1 ; 2 4]=6·4-1·2=24-2=22; the bed's area is 22 square metres. (a).

questions.explanation: Swapping the two columns changes the sign of a determinant, so the value becomes -22 (the area itself stays 22). (c).

questions.q: Replacing v by which vector would flatten the bed to zero area?
questions.explanation: Zero area needs v parallel to u=(6,2), i.e. v=λ u. Since (3,1)=\tfrac12(6,2), choosing v=(3,1) flattens the bed. (b).
